commits.message:
Space UI: Jobs — scheduled and manual jobs in plain language (#138)

* space-ui: Jobs — scheduled and manual jobs in plain language

Setup's Commands section becomes Jobs. New job asks first whether the job
is Scheduled (runs on its own) or Manual (saved to run with Run now), then
shows only the fields that kind needs.

- Schedules are chosen in words: every N seconds/minutes/hours/days, every
  hour at a minute, every day at a time, or every week on a day at a time,
  with a live preview of the schedule and first run. The time limit reads
  "Stop it if a run takes longer than N seconds/minutes/hours" (5 minutes
  for a new job). Rows carry a Scheduled/Manual badge, the schedule in
  words and the status in words.
- core/jobs.js (no DOM, no network) maps those choices onto the existing
  every_seconds + first_run_at fields and back, so /api/schedules, the
  stored jobs and agents using the API are unchanged. Editing reopens a job
  as the choice that produced it and can switch its kind.
- Inbox Jobs lists manual jobs too and gains Run now.
- The UI label changes only: route #/setup/commands and DOM ids stay.
  The panel's log path is corrected to ~/.quirq/logs/scheduler/<id>.log.

* space-ui: Jobs editor shows what sets each kind apart first, in its own card

Picking Scheduled or Manual used to reveal the same Name/Description fields
first, with the schedule far below, and the form sat inside the list card
behind one thin line.

- New job and Edit open a separate New job card above Your jobs, with its
  own header and a close button.
- Scheduled goes straight to "When should it run?": four preset tiles with
  icons (Every..., Hourly, Daily, Weekly) showing only the chosen tile's
  inputs, a 7-day strip from today marking each day's run time or run count
  (on Weekly a day in the strip picks it), and the next three runs.
- Manual shows a "No schedule" panel explaining that it runs on Run now.
- "What should it run?" (name, command, folder, time limit) follows for both.
- core/jobs.js gains upcomingRuns and runsPerDay for the preview; runs per
  day are counted arithmetically, so frequent intervals cost nothing extra.
- Form errors show in the editor card, list and run errors in the list card.

* jobs: Repeating and One time, with a shadcn calendar and a start date

A job now either repeats or runs once, and both kinds pick dates on a
calendar.

- Scheduler: every_seconds null with first_run_at is a one-time job. The
  tick runs it once at that time (a past time at once), clears next_run
  and keeps the job and its history; saving it with the same time does not
  run it again, a new time does. Without first_run_at it stays Run now only.
  A due one-time run waits for a free runner instead of being skipped.
- Setup: the kinds are Repeating and One time. "When should it run?" comes
  first for both, with the calendar: Repeating picks an optional start date
  (days that get a run are dotted; a custom interval with a start also asks
  for the first run's time), One time picks the day plus a time, or no day
  to wait for Run now. Past times are refused except a job's saved one.
- core/shadcn.js gains calendar() and wireCalendar(), a port of shadcn's
  Calendar (react-day-picker markup, --cell-size, today/selected/outside/
  disabled states, arrow-key navigation); css/shadcn.css styles it.
- core/jobs.js: start dates for presets, onceToFields, jobToOnce,
  startForJob, describeOnce.
- Inbox Jobs badges read Repeating / One time.

* space-ui: radios in the Jobs form lose the text-input box and square focus glow

The form's input rule (width, padding, border, background) also matched its
radio buttons, and the page's input:focus glow drew a square around the one
the editor focuses on open. Radios now reset those properties; keyboard focus
rings the whole Repeating/One time or preset tile instead.

Fix connections signed_in for bring-your-own-key mode (#151)

* Fix connections signed_in for bring-your-own-key mode

service.signed_in() (used by GET /api/connections and the Inbox 'not signed in'
state) still checked the XO token via get_auth_token(). In BYO mode there is no
XO token, so connections reported 'not signed in' even with a valid Composio key.
Check byo_key.configured() instead — the key is what the poller needs to reach

* Don't show stale gating errors on a connection

poller records them as last_error and they only clear on the next poll. Between
enabling a toolkit (or adding a key) and that poll, the drawer showed an error
contradicting the card ('On in this workspace'). Recompute the gate at read time
in _entry so a stale gating error is suppressed; real provider/collector errors
are always shown.

commits.message:
Fix codex chat history dropping every user turn (#162)

* Fix codex chat history dropping every user turn

Newer codex builds no longer write the legacy event_msg/user_message
event; a user turn is recorded only as a response_item message with role
"user". The rollout converter built user bubbles from that event alone
and explicitly skipped non-assistant response_items, so history rendered
assistant text and tool chips with every user message missing, and
consecutive assistant turns merged into a single block.

Read the user turn from both rollout shapes, collapsing the pair on
builds that emit each one so a turn never renders twice. Resolve the
user line before a_ts is set, so it cannot stamp the assistant message
that follows it with the user's timestamp. Strip injected
<environment_context> and <user_instructions> wrappers by explicit tag
rather than a leading "<", so a genuine prompt starting with a tag still
reaches the transcript.

enrich_project_session read the same dead event, which left every codex
session titled "Untitled Session"; it now takes the title from the same
prompt source as the bubbles.

* Tell codex's injected context from the typed turn by its own label

Codex sends a user turn's injected context — plugin recommendations,
AGENTS.md, environment context — as a separate role:"user" message, so
the transcript has to pick the right message rather than render both.
The first pass matched context blocks by tag name, which missed
<recommended_plugins> and, worse, could have truncated a future prompt
that happened to match the pattern.

Codex labels every block itself:
internal_chat_message_metadata_passthrough.content_item_kinds runs
parallel to content, reading ["user.text"] on a typed turn against
["plugins.recommendations", "agents_md.instructions",
"environments.environment_context"] on an injected one. Select blocks in
the user.* namespace and drop the rest — codex's equivalent of the
isMeta flag claude_code already reads.

Blocks are now chosen, never rewritten, so no prompt can be truncated or
mangled whatever it contains, and a context kind codex adds later is
excluded without a code change. Labels that are absent, malformed, or
not parallel to content fall back to the previous whole-message rule
instead of blanking the turn, so older rollouts and the legacy
event_msg shape still convert.

commits.message:
Index sessions started without a project (#146) (#180)

* Index sessions started without a project (#146)

A chat with neither agent_id nor workspace runs in the projects root. Since
#82 its index row went to write_session_row("default", ...), which refuses
when no default/ folder exists, and nothing logged the refusal, so the
session was missing from /api/sessions, empty in /api/messages and a 404
on /transcript.

Such a session now has no project id at all: an empty project segment in
its key (claude::web:<hex>), which no folder can ever match, and its rows
at the Space level, ~/.quirq/sessions/sessionslist.d/, outside the
per-project ~/.quirq/projects/<key>/ namespace. Nothing is reserved that a
project could be named; "default" is an ordinary project name.

- storage/layout.py: sessions_dir() (~/.quirq/sessions/), one folder per
  subject like the others.
- engine/sessions_io.py: an empty name at the seam is the projects root;
  read_root_session_index(); iter_project_session_indexes yields it first
  as ("", <projects root>, rows) so every reader (list, messages owner,
  transcript, PATCH directory) sees these sessions; a refused write is
  logged with the session key instead of dropped silently.
- claude_code, codex, antigravity adapters: key project-less sessions with
  an empty segment, run them in the projects root, no "default" literal.
- workspace/sessionslist.py: the union includes the root index.
- tests/test_root_sessions.py: the #146 acceptance (a project-less stream
  leaves a row both readers find, no project name can reach that index, a
  refused write is logged); the state-root fixture gains sessions/.

openclaw and hermes are unchanged: openclaw's project-less sessions list
through its native store, hermes' agent_id is a profile, not a project.

* Hold the Space UI to the cache-stamp rule instead of pinning stamp values

Three tests pinned literal ?v= stamps (api.js at 20260914-files2, base.css
at the footer stamp, and a diary of which change moved which file). Every
legitimate bump broke them, which #168 did and #170 re-pinned, while the
one failure that matters, a module the browser can keep serving stale, was
never checked.

The tests now assert the rule the stamps exist for, with no stamp value
anywhere in them: every stylesheet and the app entry carry a stamp and
exist; every relative import across space_ui/js is either stamped by its
importer or bare and rewritten by the import map, never both and never
neither; the import map sits ahead of app.js and maps at least api.js,
ui.js and connections.js; no importer stamps a mapped module itself.

Holding the tree to that rule found two gaps: core/store.js and
core/markdown.js are imported bare by six files but were not in the import
map, so a cached copy was never refreshed. Both are mapped now, which is
the mechanism index.html already documents for shared core modules.
commits.author: KrishBhimani

Archive the command log under inbox/activity and move state migrations to their own module

The shared commands.log kept one old generation: at 5 MB it became
commands.log.1 and the previous .1 was deleted, so older history was lost.
At 5 MB the log now moves to archive/commands.<UTC stamp>.log and a fresh
log starts. Nothing deletes, compresses or caps the archive.

The log and its archive live under the Space UI page they belong to,
~/.quirq/inbox/activity/. New state in ~/.quirq/ goes under
<section>/<page>/ from now on, ahead of a refactor of the whole layout
into projects, agents, inbox and setup.

- utils/commands: rotation archives instead of overwriting .1. Archive
  names sort in time order; a taken stamp steps forward a second. Until
  the boot migration runs, a copy at an old path keeps being appended to.
- utils/runtime_env: inbox_activity_dir(), beside logs_dir(), because
  utils/ may not import services/.
- services/storage/migrations.py (new): Move, migrate_layout() and MOVES
  move out of layout.py, which now only names where files live. MOVES
  holds one commented block per layout change.
- Upgrading installs: every old copy of the log (commands.log,
  commands.log.1, logs/commands.log, logs/commands.log.1) moves into the
  archive, named for its last write, and the live log starts fresh. An
  archive name is always free, so the result does not depend on whether
  something wrote to the new path first.
- plugins/quirq/scripts/space.sh: the Codex launcher's CLI check sets the
  state root for itself only and no longer passes QUIRQ_COMMAND_LOG_PATH to
  the server, where it read as the user's choice and pinned the log. A path
  the user set is still passed on. Installs still running a launcher from

commits.message:
Composio: run blocking SDK calls off the event loop (#163) (#164)

The Composio SDK is synchronous, and the router and the MCP proxy called it
straight from async handlers. While one call waited on Composio, the whole
server stopped answering.

- Router and MCP proxy run every Composio network call through
  asyncio.to_thread. Handlers stay async: kick_gateway_sweep() needs the
  running loop. Request and response shapes are unchanged.
- get_session, sync_session and invalidate_session share one lock now that
  they can overlap on worker threads; without it two callers could both mint
  a session and leak one. A cached session is still returned without waiting
  on the lock.
- A session replaced inside get_session is queued for the sweep to delete
  instead of being dropped, off the agent's tool-call path.
- mcp_config docstring names xo-space, not the pre-rename service.
commits.author: KrishBhimani

commits.message:
Add xo-doctor: a read-only health check for Quirq state (#187)

* feat(storage): name the quarantine/ folder of the state root

xo-doctor moves leftover runtime data aside instead of deleting it. The
folder is named once in layout.py, like every other subject folder, and
the golden sample gains an example so the layout test keeps them equal.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* feat(doctor): classify state files into one read outcome

The shared read helpers put permission errors, empty files and parse
errors into one bucket, so a transient error looks like corruption. The
doctor needs them apart: unreadable is reported on its own, and a bad
file written in the last 5 seconds is not judged.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* feat(doctor): inventory of state files and accepted schema versions

The doctor must judge a file by how much it matters and by which schema
versions this xo-space reads. The fixtures are the truth but don't ship
in the Docker image, so the inventory reads the shipped schema files and
keeps a small version table that tests hold equal to the fixtures.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(doctor): bound walk_files by directories as well as files

The walk_files limit was only checked against file counts, allowing
directory-heavy trees to walk far past the limit and never set truncated=True.
Fixed to count directories and files equally in the limit check, matching
the behavior of reading.measure_tree and ensuring the limit bounds the
total walk cost.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* feat(doctor): run read checks over the state and projects roots

Nothing reports a corrupt, unreadable or wrongly versioned state file
today; stores either refuse it or silently treat it as empty. The runner
reads every known file once, judges it by its class, isolates a failing
check as ERROR, and is held to writing nothing by a snapshot test.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* feat(doctor): report a lost Space identity and duplicate project pids

One boot without XO_SPACE_ID writes xo_space_id: null (F1), and two
folders sharing a pid silently merge their runtime data (F2). Neither is
visible today. Both are reported; nothing is changed.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* feat(doctor): report stale temp files, old layout, legacy files, a stalled watcher and growth

Interrupted writes leave temp files nobody cleans up (F4), an older server
can keep writing the old layout, and several files grow without limit.
All are reported with advice; the watcher check reuses the Quirq view's
liveness rule so the page never disagrees with itself.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* feat(doctor): detect runtime data no project uses

Removing a project leaves ~/.quirq/projects/<pid>/ behind (F3). The
doctor lists it, but offers no action while a project.json can't be read,
the projects root looks unmounted, or leftovers are as many as projects:
in each case live data could look abandoned.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(doctor): treat a partly unreadable runtime folder as undated

measure_tree used os.walk without onerror, so a subdirectory it
couldn't list (e.g. chmod 000) was silently skipped and a failed
per-entry lstat was swallowed by a bare continue. Tree.newest still
reported the parent's stale mtime and truncated stayed False, so
too_recent() could pass on an incomplete walk: a folder with a
just-written file under an unreadable subdirectory looked old and got
offered for a move. Spec §9.1 rule 6 requires the rule to fail when the
age can't be known.

measure_tree now records any os.walk or lstat error and returns
newest=None whenever one happened, alongside the existing None on
hitting the entry limit; bytes/files still reflect whatever was
counted. leftovers._finding's undated text changes from "Too large to
date." to "Can't be dated: too large or partly unreadable." to cover
both cases.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* feat(doctor): move a leftover runtime folder into quarantine on request

The doctor's one action. It re-checks every leftover rule at action time,
then renames the folder into quarantine/runtime-leftovers/. A rename can't
half-finish, a person can move it back, and a cross-filesystem move is
refused rather than copied.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(doctor): turn filesystem errors during move-aside into a service error

measure_tree() stat'd its root with an unguarded os.lstat, so a leftover
folder removed between listing and measuring (a person emptying it, a
concurrent move of another key) raised a raw FileNotFoundError out of
survey() — and the same call backs the GET report's runtime check. A
non-searchable projects/ could also raise EACCES out of Path.is_dir() /
is_symlink() in move_aside(). Task 9's router only catches ServiceError,
so either one would have surfaced as an unstructured 500 instead of the
doctor's typed failure shape (architecture §9.3).

commits.message:
fix(space): guard every write against cross-site browser requests (#139)

* fix(space): guard every write against cross-site browser requests

PR #127 added the origin/rebinding check but called it per route, so it
covered about 10 of the 158 POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE routes. Review of #127
demonstrated the gap: a page on another origin cross-site submitted a
multipart form to POST /api/files/upload and the server wrote the file.
Uploads, secrets, chat, config, channels, connectors and the visualizer
writes were all unguarded.

server.py now installs BrowserWriteGuard on every write, before the CORS
middleware so it runs inside CORS and a refusal still carries CORS headers.
A write is accepted when:

- it carries no Origin and no cross-site Sec-Fetch-Site: a CLI, an agent, or
  another app's server-side proxy (xo-swarm reaches Space this way);
- its Origin is an ALLOWED_ORIGINS entry, a frontend this API already trusts
  to read its replies (xo-coworker desktop and remote mode). "*" and "null"
  never count for writes;
- origin_allowed passes: the Origin is the address the request was sent to,
  and not one DNS rebinding can reach (unchanged from #127);
- the TCP peer is loopback and the Origin is the X-Forwarded-Host address: a
  frontend's own server proxying to Space. Next.js rewrites set Host to the
  target, X-Forwarded-Host to the host the browser used, and pass Origin
  through unchanged (verified in next/dist .../proxy-request.ts at the
  version xo-coworker locks). A cross-site page cannot add that header
  without a CORS preflight, and a remote caller is not a loopback peer.

Everything else is 403 with an actionable detail, before the route runs.
GET and OPTIONS are untouched, so CORS preflights and reads are unaffected.
The per-route checks stay as the stricter extra on the routes that run
programs or control the server.

No exempt list: the OAuth callbacks are GET redirects, and the POST
"callbacks" (claude-code, antigravity, vercel oauth/exchange) carry a code
the user pasted into our own UI.

Verified under WSL with the repo venv and AGENT_NAME=claude_code: the new
tests failed first (guard absent, wiring absent). tests.test_browser_guard
plus the existing guard suites (scheduler_api, space_restart,
project_management) pass, 67 tests. Full tests/ discover: 1296 tests, only
the 9 known Windows line-ending failures. `import server` passes for
claude_code and openclaw with middleware order RecordTransportClient,
ProxyHeadersMiddleware, CORSMiddleware, BrowserWriteGuard. tests2: the same
3 failures as untouched development (two hermes literals in core, the
presenter I/O rule), none from this change. A real uvicorn on a socket,
wired as server.py does, accepted the CLI, Space-page, frontend-proxy and
trusted-origin shapes and refused the cross-site multipart upload and a
forged X-Forwarded-Host, with the route never running.

Not covered here: the files.py path-clamping bugs (separate fix(files) PR),
Docker command writes (the bridge address is not loopback), and chat, which
can still run programs on behalf of anyone who reaches the page.

* fix(space): confine file paths and listen on loopback unless HOST says otherwise

Two findings from the review of this PR, both about who can reach the
file API and where it can write.

Files. POST /api/files/upload wrote wherever the request said: the
workspace form field was resolved with no home check, and the filename was
joined as sent. A "../x" name climbed out of the folder, and an absolute
name discarded the folder entirely (Path(dir) / "/abs/x" is "/abs/x"). The
other five routes did clamp to home, but with str(target).startswith(home),
so a sibling such as /home/user-shared passed as inside /home/user; mkdir's
extra-file check had the same prefix test, six in all.

- _within(base, target) decides containment on resolved paths with
  relative_to, and replaces all six prefix checks.
- upload is confined to home or xo_projects_root(). Docker keeps projects at
  /workspace/xo-projects with home /root, so home alone would break uploads
  there. Both frontends upload inside those roots: xo-swarm sends the home
  directory, xo-coworker a project or session folder.
- upload keeps only Path(filename).name ("upload" for an empty, "." or ".."
  name) and re-checks the final file path before reading or writing it, so a
  symlink already at that name cannot lead the write outside.

Listen address. install.sh writes HOST=127.0.0.1, but server.py and
cowork-api.sh fell back to 0.0.0.0 and .env.example showed 0.0.0.0. So a
.env copied from the example, a .env without a HOST line (including a restart
from Setup, which goes through cowork-api.sh), or `python server.py` listened
on every interface. The API has no login, and a non-browser request carries
no Origin, so any device on the same network could read and change the
user's files. Both fall back to 127.0.0.1 now, and .env.example and the
README say what 0.0.0.0 exposes. The Docker image relied on the old default,
so the Dockerfile sets ENV HOST=0.0.0.0: inside a container that is correct,
and compose.local.yml still publishes 127.0.0.1 only.

Verified under WSL with the repo venv and AGENT_NAME=claude_code: the new
tests failed first, including a real write outside the target folder through
an absolute filename. tests.test_files_paths and tests.test_browser_guard
pass (21 tests). Full tests/ discover: 1306 tests, only the 9 known Windows
line-ending failures. `import server` passes for claude_code and openclaw;
cowork-api.sh passes bash -n. In the local tests2 suite, the strict xfail that
recorded the sibling-prefix hole now passes, as intended.

* docs(docker): point the HOST comment at -p 127.0.0.1, not the removed compose file

Add Grok Bot adapter (`AGENT_NAME=grokbot`) (#186)

* Add Grok Bot Plane-B adapter (AGENT_NAME=grokbot)

Drop config/agents/grokbot and adapters/grokbot so Space can chat through
a running Grok Bot host gateway and list sand-data transcript JSONL.
No core router or service files are named. README and .env.example list
the new backend and its gateway / sand-data env keys.

Co-authored-by: quirqy <quirq-dev@users.noreply.github.com>

* Fix Grok Bot dispatch, session ownership, and stale follow-up replies

Load the adapter through the real dispatcher and persist Space-to-host identity
before sending prompts so chats survive refreshes. Fence replies to the current
prompt and fail on timeout instead of replaying a previous answer.

Reuse the HTTP client with polling backoff, attempt host interruption on cancel,
clean up standalone seats, and preserve user-envelope tool results. Document
host-managed features and lifecycle limits rather than advertising full parity.

* Fix Grok Bot completion and history for the live gateway

Acceptance may remain not-found after a successful run, and current hosts
serve transcripts through the gateway rather than JSONL files. Require an
idle seat plus nonce/requestId-correlated replies, and reopen Space chats
through paginated gateway history. Use live-probe fixtures and document
host placement, text-only history, and Space-owned secret storage.

* Keep Grok Bot history reads usable when the gateway is unavailable

Return empty history and log redacted gateway errors so stopped hosts or
missing tokens do not turn recurring message reads into HTTP 500s. Scope
reply validation to the current nonce so app and automation entries without
correlation keys cannot break a shared-seat turn. Cover both history HTTP
routes, token-free logging, and mixed transcripts with regression tests.

* Use adapter health so gateway-only agents are not reported missing in Setup

An empty manifest binary means no CLI is required. Report it as not applicable and check the active adapter's health with a five-second deadline, preserving local checks for CLI agents. Keep Setup available on health failures and avoid requiring local host files for a remote service.

Cover API and Setup states, retain the visible activity limitations, and record the reviewer's successful live chat validation.

commits.message:
fix(projects, sharing): removal no longer depends on sharing; restore prefills; bound the relay's git calls (#199)

* fix(projects): removing a local project no longer depends on sharing

Removal deleted only this Space's copy, yet it asked the swarm who the repo
was shared with and blocked on the answer. The swarm answers 403 for a repo
nobody shared, so every never-shared GitHub project was stuck behind
"Sharing could not be verified", and a Space outside a sharing group was
told to get the owner to revoke everyone before deleting its own clone.

Removal now skips the membership check. Local safety checks, the
collaborator roster, the origin re-check and the relay's removal marker
(which stops the relay from cloning the folder back) are unchanged.
`members` stays in the removal response, always empty.

* feat(sharing): "Clone project" on a removed repo prefills the Add form

Inbox → Sharing lists a repo removed from this Space with a "Clone project"
button, which opened Manage's Add form empty although the repo was known.
It now passes the repository URL (https://<repo>.git, as the relay clones),
and the form suggests the folder name from it as it does for typed URLs.
The form is filled only when empty, so a draft in progress is kept, and
cloning still needs a click. Cache stamps are bumped for the changed modules.

* fix(sharing): bound the relay's git calls so a hang can't stall the loop

git fetch and git ls-remote ran with no timeout, so one hung network call
froze the relay for every repo until a restart. Every git call in git_ops
now has one: 300 s for fetch (a large pack can't resume, so it gets room),
60 s for ls-remote and 60 s for local reads. On a timeout the runner kills
git and its helpers, and the call fails like any other git error, so the
relay records it and retries on the next tick.

fetch and ls-remote also run with GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0 for that command
only, as clone already did: without credentials git fails at once instead
of waiting on a username prompt. With a credential helper nothing changes.

* docs(env): sharing bookmarks live in <state>/sharing/

feat(quirq): show the full Space UI in ChatGPT/Codex sidebar, panel and chat (#200)

* feat(quirq): add MCP server with compact Space dashboard for ChatGPT/Codex

Bundle a local stdio MCP server with the quirq Codex plugin: read-only
tools for projects, project details and active sessions, a compact MCP App
dashboard with sidebar (global) and conversation (thread) entrypoints, a
demo mode, a packager for upload/marketplace ZIPs and hermetic tests.

* feat(quirq): show the full Space UI in ChatGPT/Codex sidebar, panel and chat

The plugin now renders the real Space UI (space_ui/, unmodified) inside the
ChatGPT desktop app instead of a separate dashboard:

- scripts/build_space_app.py bundles space_ui's markup, CSS, fonts and ES
  modules (esbuild) plus ui/space-bridge.js into one MCP App view,
  ui/space-app.html. The view is generated but committed, since the GitHub
  marketplace installs this folder from git; a freshness test fails while it
  is stale against its sources.
- ui/space-bridge.js does the MCP Apps handshake and replaces fetch for Space
  URLs: requests travel as space_api_read / space_api_write tool calls to the
  MCP server, which forwards them to the local Space. It also handles links
  (native opener, ui/open-link, copy fallback), deep links, hash routing and
  shares the visible page with the conversation (background context, "+ Chat").
- mcp/server.py: sidebar (global) and conversation panel (thread) entrypoints
  plus space_open for any Space page; app-only proxy tools with a path
  allowlist, header allowlist, size caps, no redirects and no server
  stop/restart/update; composer @-mentions with xo-space:// project, inbox and
  active-session resources; structured plugin settings; space_inbox and
  space_status; honest results for hosts that cannot display views.
- skills: onboarding skill (manifest onboardingSkill); start/install open Space
  in the app with the link as fallback and explain how long Space keeps running.
- Plugin version 1.5.0; EXTENSIONS.md documents design, build and limits.

* test(quirq): move plugin tests to tests/ and keep them out of the plugin

The tests shipped inside plugins/quirq (the ZIP and every marketplace install)
and the repo's own test run never executed them.

- tests/test_quirq_space_view.py (stdlib): the committed Space view is fresh
  against space_ui/ and the bridge; the upload ZIP contents (no tests/).
  Runs in every test run, where a space_ui change would make it stale.
- tests/test_quirq_plugin_server.py: the MCP server tests. They need the
  plugin's pinned mcp 1.x, so they skip (with the uv command) under mcp 2.x.
- tests/test_quirq_bridge.py runs tests/quirq/check_bridge.cjs when Node is
  available.
- Remove the manual smoke scripts check_ui.cjs (Playwright) and
  check_http.py; package_plugin.py no longer zips tests/.
- .gitattributes marks the generated ui/space-app.html as linguist-generated
  so GitHub collapses it in diffs.

* fix(quirq): enforce the proxy policy in the server, on the canonical route

The app-only visibility of space_api_read/space_api_write is a host hint,
not a boundary: a host that ignores it (Codex CLI, other MCP clients) lets
the model call the proxy, and Space trusts its requests as a local client.

- The server now refuses, for any caller: reading secret values; changing
  secrets, provider keys or the Composio key; jobs (they run local commands);
  Space chat; runtime config and restart; doctor actions; project sharing
  (share, revoke, apply, peers); deleting projects; server stop, restart and
  update. Everyday Space UI reads and changes keep working.
- Rules match the canonical route (decoded once as Space's server decodes it,
  slashes collapsed, no trailing slash), so percent-encoded variants such as
  /space/server/re%73tart no longer bypass the deny list. A path that only
  decodes into an allowed prefix is rejected.

* fix(quirq): forward only the routes the Space UI uses (default deny)

The proxy's deny list was default-allow: every Space route it did not name
was forwarded, including file read/write under $HOME (/api/files/*), skill
installs, connector token writes and /api/xo-projects-sync. Hosts may ignore
the app-only visibility hint, so the proxy is now an allowlist of exactly the
routes space_ui/js calls, matched on the canonical route:

- reads for every Space page (secrets: names only, never values);
- everyday changes: theme/branding, inbox status, project creation,
  connection settings and polling, telemetry sources.

Everything else (secret values, files, jobs, sharing, project deletion,
connector credentials, workspace config, server control, any future route)
is refused with "not available from ChatGPT; open Space in your browser".
Loading all 21 Space pages through the bridge against a live Space made 25
distinct requests; none is refused.

* docs(quirq): document the uv requirement for the MCP server

* refactor(quirq): remove demo mode from the plugin

QUIRQ_EXTENSION_DEMO made the MCP server answer from hardcoded sample
projects, sessions, todos and inbox items, and the compact dashboard had
its own ?demo=1 sample. Test scaffolding does not belong in what users
install, so both are gone: the plugin only ever shows real Space data.

The server tests now patch a small fake Space inside the test file, and

The repo's one-executor rule (tests/test_command_executor.py) forbids
importing subprocess outside utils/commands. The build script now calls
utils.commands.run_sync, imported on use because the shipped plugin

* docs(quirq): run Space through WSL when Codex runs on Windows

Space runs on Linux or macOS only. When Codex runs on Windows, the quirq

which bash cannot run, and the start skill had the agent poll /health,

Keep only the previous command log when QUIRQ_COMMAND_LOG_ARCHIVE=false (#232)

* Keep only the previous command log on a release

A development checkout keeps every full commands.log in
inbox/activity/archive/, which nothing deletes. On a release that grows
without bound on machines nobody watches, so a release now keeps one
earlier generation instead: at 5 MB the log replaces commands.log.1, and
the two files never take more than about 10 MB.

A release is a checkout whose HEAD is exactly a vX.Y.Z tag (RELEASING.md),
asked once per process with `git tag --points-at HEAD`. When git cannot
answer (no checkout, no git) the install gets the bounded log.
QUIRQ_COMMAND_LOG_ARCHIVE=on|off overrides the checkout.

Until installs follow tags, every install is on a branch, so behaviour is
unchanged.

* Choose the command log archive with QUIRQ_COMMAND_LOG_ARCHIVE alone

Images ship without .git, so a git probe cannot tell a release from a
development build. Drop it: QUIRQ_COMMAND_LOG_ARCHIVE=true (the default)
keeps every full commands.log in inbox/activity/archive/ as before, and
false keeps only the previous one as commands.log.1.

* Tidy the command log rotation text and make the .1 helper private

The _iter_log_paths docstring and the Setup label said "archived" for
both modes; they now say rotated. _previous_command_log_path is only used
inside the module. A comment at the .1 replace records the cross-process
race the per-process lock cannot prevent.

commits.message:
fix(doctor): report only what is true, and what the stores refuse (#230)

* fix(doctor): report documents that parse but their store can't use

The doctor judged a file healthy once it parsed and carried an accepted
schema number. A todos.json whose sessions is a list, a workitems.json
whose items is a list, a peers.json listing a user twice, or a
scheduler jobs.json whose jobs is a list all passed, while the stores
refuse them (todos and work items stop saving, collaborator requests
and project removal fail, no scheduled command runs). An inbox.json
whose items is not a list loads as empty, and the next write replaces
every saved item; that passed too.

Each of those stores now exposes its existing rule as a pure
shape_problem(document) and calls it where it validated inline, so its
behaviour and messages are unchanged. The Inbox store stays lenient;
its shape_problem only names what normalize_document would drop.

A new content check (after read) asks each owning store that question
for every file that parsed, and reports content.wrong_shape with the
store's reason as evidence and the catalog's wrong_shape/wrong_type
texts. Stores are imported inside the check, so a renamed function
costs only this check. The scheduler liveness check no longer goes
silent without a report when jobs or state is not an object.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(inbox): refuse to overwrite an inbox.json whose items would be lost

load_document read an inbox.json whose items is not a list, or whose
whole document is not an object, as an empty Inbox with ok=True. The
next refresh or change then wrote that empty Inbox back over the file,
so every saved item, seen and done mark and note was lost.

Such a file is now not ok, exactly like one that is not valid JSON:
reads still show an empty Inbox, refresh skips it, and modify refuses
with scope_unavailable (the message now says the items may be the
problem). The file is never rewritten. An inbox.json with no items key
yet is still a usable, empty Inbox.

The doctor's Inbox text follows: the wrong-type and wrong-shape cases
now say the Inbox shows empty and changes fail, instead of warning that
the next refresh overwrites it.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(doctor): report saved commands that can't run while the watcher is off

The watcher is the only caller of scheduler.tick(), so with
QUIRQ_WATCHER_ENABLED=false an enabled saved command never runs. Both
the watcher and scheduler checks returned nothing in that case: on a
live server, a command five days overdue was reported as healthy.

The scheduler check now reports scheduler.not_running when the watcher
is off and enabled commands exist: WARN, or FAIL once one is already
past due, with the most overdue command as evidence. Turning the
watcher off is a setting a person may choose in Setup, so on its own it
is only an OK note (watcher.disabled), which the Health panel doesn't
show as a problem; the scheduler finding is not folded under it, since
a warning inside an OK row would be hidden.

Verified with a live server (watcher off, a command due since January):
scheduler.not_running FAIL naming the command.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(doctor): say whether XO refused the key, errored, or couldn't be reached

relay.unreachable told a person to check their network for every failed
poll: swarm_api.project_sharing.poll returned None for any failure and
the relay kept no status. On a live server with XO answering 401, the
usage check said "XO refused this Space's API key" while the relay
check, about the same 401, said "check this machine's network".

The swarm client gains poll_detailed() -> (body, status, offline); poll()
is now a thin wrapper with the same contract. The relay poller uses it
and records last_poll_status / last_poll_offline in its status snapshot
(additive), and its log line names the cause. The doctor maps one rule
for every XO caller (liveness.xo_failure): offline -> relay.unreachable,
401/403 or nothing to authenticate with -> relay.rejected, any other
answer -> relay.xo_error, unknown -> relay.failed, which claims no cause.

Usage reporting already recorded an inconclusive key check as
"unverified" with the HTTP status (or none when XO wasn't reached); the
doctor ignored it for 26 hours. It now reports usage.xo_error or
usage.unreachable.

Relay tests that mocked poll() now mock poll_detailed(). Verified on a
live server against a local fake XO: 401, 500 and no listener give
rejected, xo_error and unreachable for both relay and usage.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(doctor): tell an empty usage record from one that stops the watcher

A stats.json or sessions-augment.json holding the wrong JSON type got
one text for every case: "the watcher fails on this file on every tick".
On a live server that is true only for a value with content. The
watcher's sinks read `read_json(path) or {}`: an empty value ([], "", 0,
false, null) reads as no file and is replaced by totals counted from the
next activity, while a list or string with content makes the step raise
each time the project has new activity. That activity, and its timeline
lines, are then never recorded, even after the file is repaired
(verified live: 8 exchanges with stats.json = [1, 2] left the timeline
and totals unchanged, and repairing the file did not bring them back).

ReadResult gains empty_value for wrong_type, and a read finding looks
up the catalog's "wrong_type_empty" situation first. Both files now say
what actually happens in each case, and urge restoring a copy soon when
activity is being lost.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(storage): never read a device, FIFO or runaway file as a state file

With scheduler/jobs.json linked to /dev/zero, a live server allocated
about 1 GB on every watcher tick until MemoryError: the scheduler read
the path with read_text(), which never ends on a device. A FIFO at a
state path would make open() wait for a writer forever.

utils/safe_read.read_text_guarded() stats the path first and refuses
anything but a regular file (a link to one is followed, as before)
without opening it, opens with O_NONBLOCK and re-checks, and caps a
document at 50 MB. Its errors subclass OSError, so callers that already
treat an unreadable file as unreadable keep their behaviour. It is used
by the readers of state documents: storage.reader.read_json and
atomic_write's stamped-document reader (most stores), the scheduler,
the session index, the reading positions, the GitHub mirror, sharing
bookmarks, theme, branding, onboarding and the Inbox's empty-file check.
Append-only logs (timelines, run histories) grow by design, so they are
checked for their kind only, with no size cap. It lives in utils/
because the scheduler sits below services/.

Two tests that faked an unreadable file by patching Path.read_text now
patch the reader those modules use. Verified live: with jobs.json ->
/dev/zero the server's memory stays flat (82-89 MB over 30 s).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(doctor): report links, FIFOs and devices at state paths

The state walk kept only regular files, so a FIFO at inbox/inbox.json
or scheduler/jobs.json linked to /dev/zero was never judged and the
report said healthy (live test D4).

walk_files() can now collect every entry that is neither a regular file
nor a real folder (links to files or folders, FIFOs, sockets, devices),
still without opening or following any of them. For a known state path:
a FIFO or device is read.special; a link to one, or to a folder, gets
the same read finding with the link target as evidence; a dangling link
is shape.symlink (FAIL where losing the file is a FAIL); a link to a
real file is shape.symlink WARN, since every store saves with
os.replace() and so replaces the link with a regular file, and the
file it points to is judged as usual. Unknown entries stay OK notes,
and logs and credentials behind links are left alone.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(doctor): correct the catalog where it misdescribes what the server does

An audit of every catalog text against the code that writes and reads
each file found five false claims and about twenty partial ones; the
user-visible ones were confirmed on a live server. Corrected:

- todos.json and cache/stats.json holding a list or string with content
  make their routes fail with HTTP 500 (`.get` on the value); an empty
  value reads as no document. Each case now says which, using the
  wrong_type_empty situation.
- cache/sessions/sessionslist.json and sessions-augment.json: nothing in
  the server reads them (Space-wide routes merge each project's index).
- projects.json is written through ChangeGate, so it is a change cache,
  not "replaced within seconds"; inventory behaviour updated.
- Change caches are also rebuilt at the next server start.
- An empty connection settings file is replaced with defaults on the
  next save; an empty or wrong-type accounts.json is rewritten by the
  next account lookup.
- Smaller corrections: what an Inbox refresh brings back; scheduler
  state needs the watcher; usage re-send needs sign-in and an accepted
  key; reading positions cover the agents that use that file; todo
  changes also rewrite session counters; session entries "usually"
  can't be resumed; a GitHub copy is rewritten by any poll and deleting
  it closes Inbox items only until each issue next changes; live
  activity with content fails its route; agent.json leaves the agent
  listed under its folder name; restoring .xo/ from git works only if
  the project commits it.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(doctor): say how much was checked, so "Healthy" means checked

A report could read healthy while parts of the state were never looked
at: the walk stops at 50,000 entries, and a check can fail to run. A
big but healthy Space also carried a permanent FAIL for its size (live
test C1).

Every report gains a coverage block (additive): files seen, documents
read, unknown files, special entries, unreadable folders, whether the
walk was truncated, the walk limit, checks that couldn't run, and
complete. read.too_large becomes a WARN, since size isn't damage, and
is pinned so the per-check cap can never drop the row that says the
report is partial. The Health panel shows "Healthy (partly checked)"
instead of "Healthy" when coverage isn't complete, and adds the number
of files read (and "not every file was checked") to the check time; a
report from an older server without coverage renders as before. The view's
cache stamp and index.html's app.js stamp move together, and the plugin's
prebuilt plugins/quirq/ui/space-app.html is rebuilt.

Verified with a live server: 52,000 extra files give a WARN report with
complete=false; the panel's real badge code, run under node on live
reports, renders each case as described.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(doctor): show "partly checked" on the badge at any level

The Health badge said "Healthy (partly checked)" only when the level was
OK. A truncated walk always adds the read.too_large WARN, and a check
that couldn't run makes the level ERROR, so that text could never be
seen: on a live server with 52,000 extra files the badge read just
"WARN" while the report's coverage said complete=false.

"(partly checked)" now follows whatever the level is: "WARN (partly
checked)" in that case, "Healthy (partly checked)" if a future cause
leaves the level at OK. Stamps moved and the plugin's prebuilt UI is
rebuilt.

fix(install): only run from a checkout nobody else can change, and stop instead of resetting it (#236)

* fix(install): never adopt a shared temp dir as the checkout

The quirq.ai bootstrap saves install.sh to a temp file and runs it, and on
Linux that file usually sits in /tmp. resolve_repo_dir took any directory
holding server.py and requirements.txt as an in-place checkout, so files
another user left in /tmp were installed and run instead of xo-space. Both
probes (the script's own directory and the launch directory) now skip a
directory that is world-writable or owned by another user, and say why.

The port probe now exits 3 for "in use", so a crash in the probe (exit 1,
e.g. an ImportError) no longer reads as "Port 5002 is already in use".

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01UzFWDRUqzEGm8fntDTH9g1

* test(install): check the launch-dir probe through looks_like_checkout

The source-text test asserted the old inline "${LAUNCH_DIR}/server.py"
check, which the previous commit moved into looks_like_checkout.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01UzFWDRUqzEGm8fntDTH9g1

* fix(install): trust a checkout by its real path, and stop instead of resetting it

The checkout probes now resolve the physical path (pwd -P) before any
check, so a symlinked checkout runs in place and macOS's /tmp link is
seen as the shared /private/tmp it points to.

A sticky world-writable folder (/tmp and the like) is never a checkout
and the install carries on in managed mode. Any other folder holding
server.py and requirements.txt must belong to the user, be writable by
nobody else (group write only for the owner's private group), carry no
ACL, and sit under folders nobody else can rename it out of. If it fails,
the installer stops with the reason and the fix (chmod go-w, setfacl -b,
or clone into a Linux folder on drives that keep no permissions) instead
of falling back to managed mode, which reset a world-writable clone to
upstream or nested a second clone in it.

The launch-dir probe adopts only a clone of the source repo, since
managed mode resets the tree, and root never adopts another user's folder
that way; root may still run another user's install.sh by path.

Harness cases cover symlinks, 0777 clones in all three launch forms,
drives without permissions, parents, group write, ACLs, another owner and
an unrelated project.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01UzFWDRUqzEGm8fntDTH9g1

* fix(install): give the managed checkout the same trust check

The one-liner's own clone was never checked: under umask 000 (common on
WSL) it made a world-writable clone and ran it, and an existing managed
checkout that others could write to, or that another user owned, was
updated and run.

Now main drops other-write from the umask before creating anything, a
fresh clone is tightened with chmod -R go-w, and the managed checkout
passes checkout_trust_problem before any git command runs in an existing
one and again after the clone. Where chmod has no effect (WSL's /mnt/c,
FAT) that stops with the Linux-folder message INSTALLATION.md describes.

Also: repo_identity lowercases first and drops user and port from the
host only, and the filesystem check reads every layer findmnt lists.

* fix(install): say chmod -R go-w when the checkout itself is writable

Clearing the stop with plain chmod go-w left every file inside the
